description.value: The study investigated neural correlates of social inclusion in females with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and healthy controls using the fMRI Cyberball paradigm.

design.value: A between-group fMRI study using a Cyberball ball-tossing paradigm with three conditions—passive watching, inclusion, and exclusion—and second-level group-by-condition analyses in 15 BPD patients, 16 MD patients, and 17 healthy controls.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I and -II)

description.value: Used to verify clinical diagnoses of major depression and borderline personality disorder.
Assessed BPD symptom severity; total scores were divided by the number of items.
Assessed current depressive symptoms using the German version.
Assessed impulsivity as a personality trait using a 30-item self-report questionnaire rated on a 4-point Likert scale.
Assessed trait rejection sensitivity, defined as anxious expectation, ready perception, and overreaction to rejection cues, using a German version.
Examined general sensitivity for social exclusion using eight questions rated on a 5-point Likert scale.
Assessed distress after social exclusion with four subscales: feeling excluded, low self-worth, meaningless existence, and control.

name.value: Feelings after fMRI visual rating scale

description.value: Subjective ratings of angry, sad, happy, afraid, frustrated, satisfied, helpless, and inner tension feelings on a scale from 1 (very low) to 4 (very strong).

source_definition.value: Data from the HC- and BPD-group were obtained by a 3T MAGNETOM Allegra and those of the MD-group by a 3T MAGNETOM Prisma Scanner.
Patients within the MD-group were significantly older than BPD-patients and HC.

description.value: Seventeen healthy controls served as control group with no current or lifetime psychiatric diagnoses.

inclusion_criteria.value: no current or lifetime psychiatric diagnoses

exclusion_criteria.value: any severe medical disorder, epilepsy, substance use disorder and psychotic disorders

recruitment_method.value: Participants were recruited from inpatient and outpatient units of the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the University Hospital Ulm.

medical_condition.value: no current or lifetime psychiatric diagnoses

medication_status.value: Smoking was prohibited at least 2 h before fMRI-scanning.

description.value: Fifteen patients were diagnosed with BPD.

inclusion_criteria.value: diagnosis of BPD verified using SCID-I and -II

exclusion_criteria.value: any severe medical disorder, epilepsy, substance use disorder and psychotic disorders

recruitment_method.value: Participants were recruited from inpatient and outpatient units of the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the University Hospital Ulm.

medical_condition.value: borderline personality disorder; 13 had comorbid major depression, 8 met criteria for PTSD, and 2 met criteria for dysthymia according DSM-IV

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I and -II)

medication_status.value: Twelve patients took antidepressants and one was medicated with lithium. Sedative drugs were disrupted prior to scanning.

description.value: Sixteen patients were diagnosed with major depressive disorder.

inclusion_criteria.value: diagnosis of MD verified using SCID-I and -II

exclusion_criteria.value: any severe medical disorder, epilepsy, substance use disorder and psychotic disorders

recruitment_method.value: Participants were recruited from inpatient and outpatient units of the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the University Hospital Ulm.

medical_condition.value: major depressive disorder; two subjects met criteria for dysthymia and one had a history of remitted anorexia

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I and -II)

medication_status.value: All MD-patients took antidepressant medication. One had concomitant topiramate, one quetiapine, and one pregabalin; these were paused for at least 3 days before fMRI scanning.

task_description.value: Participants took part in a virtual ball-tossing game with two other participants supposedly in another room. Participants were represented by a hand and the other players by animated comic figures; in fact, participants played against the computer and all actions were pre-programmed.

instructions.value: During passive watching, participants were asked just to watch the game and the computer controlled their character.

stimuli.value: A virtual ball-tossing game with animated comic figures.

task_performance_measures.value: Subjective emotional experience after fMRI, rated for angry, sad, happy, afraid, frustrated, satisfied, helpless, and inner tension.

instrument.value: 3T MAGNETOM Allegra (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany) for HC and BPD; 3T MAGNETOM Prisma Scanner (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany) for MD

description.value: T2*-sensitive gradient echo sequence; echo time 33 ms; flip angle 90°; field of view 230 mm; slice thickness 2.5 mm; interslice gap 0.5 mm; 35 transversal slices; image size 64 × 64 pixels; cyberball task.
Anatomical high-resolution T1-weighted images were acquired for coregistration and normalization into standardized stereotactic space.

Data from each session were pre-processed including slice-timing, realignment, and normalization into a standard template (MNI) with a spatial resolution of 2 × 2 × 2 mm3. Smoothing was applied with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel.

software.value: Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM12, Wellcome Department, London, United Kingdom)

steps.value: normalization into a standard MNI template with a spatial resolution of 2 × 2 × 2 mm3
smoothing with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: The cyberball task was modeled as three separate blocks of condition—passive watching, inclusion and exclusion—with six motion parameters integrated into the design matrix. Intrinsic autocorrelations were accounted for by AR(1) and low frequency drifts were removed via high-pass filtering (1/128s).

estimator.value: random effects model for group analyses

model_settings.value: The two factors were group (HC, BPD, MD) and condition (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion), including first-level contrasts for the three ball tossing conditions for each group. Scanner type and age were included as covariates in further analyses.

description.value: Participants were asked just to watch the game and the computer controlled their character.
Participants had random ball possession in one third of tosses.
The session started with 10 throws of 30% randomized ball possession and then participants were excluded from the game for the remaining 50 throws.

definition.value: A 3 × 3 ANOVA model (omnibus F-test) with the two factors “group” (HC, BPD, MD) and “condition” (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion), with group-by-condition interaction effects examined for differential neural activation under social inclusion versus passive watching.

multiple_comparison_method.value: family-wise error (FWE) correction on cluster level

interpretations.value: Group-by-condition interaction effects within the dorsolateral and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, temporo-parietal junction, posterior cingulate cortex and precuneus.

definition.value: Post hoc computed single tailed t-interaction contrasts comparing differential (social inclusion vs. passive watching) neural activations between BPD and HC, testing BPD > HC.

interpretations.value: Differential neural activations within the dmPFC, TPJ and PCC were enhanced in BPD compared to HC under social inclusion vs. passive watching conditions.

definition.value: Post hoc computed single tailed t-interaction contrasts comparing differential (social inclusion vs. passive watching) neural activations between BPD and MD, testing BPD > MD.

interpretations.value: Differential neural activations within the dmPFC, PCC and precuneus were enhanced in BPD even when compared to MD.

title.value: Results of demographic and psychometric measurements in the healthy control (HC), borderline personality disorder (BPD) and major depression (MD) group.

caption.value: Results of demographic and psychometric measurements in the healthy control (HC), borderline personality disorder (BPD) and major depression (MD) group.

footer.value: BDI, Beck Depression Inventory; BIS, Barratt Impulsiveness Scale; BSL, Borderline Symptom List; HFS, Hurt Feeling Scale; NTS, Need Threat Scale; RSQ, Rejection Sensitivity Questionnaire; numeric scales of “feelings after fMRI” range from 1 (very low) to 4 (very strong); SD, standard deviation; vs., versus; ANOVA, analysis of variance. To control for multiple comparison of the ANOVAs in dependent measures (NTS and feelings after fMRI); a false-discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied significant at p < 0.05 (FDR-corrected) to interfere significant main effects ( * ). For better demonstrational purposes, we provide measures of effect sizes (Hedges g* ) for post hoc comparisons. Please note, positive values of effect sizes reflect higher scores for BPD when comparing HC vs. BPD, and higher scores for MD when comparing HC vs. MD and BPD vs. MD. Moreover, please consider the coding for the NTS-scale: scores range from 1 (very high distress) to 5 (no distress). ( + ) denotes significant (p < 0.05) differences in post hoc comparisons (Newman Keuls). Readers are reminded that all state measures (NTS and feelings after fMRI) had been taken after the end of the whole cyber-ball paradigm.
